claim: Given a .docx package and an exact text-node value that occurs exactly once in word/document.xml, produce a package in which that single text node is replaced and every other package member is byte-identical; when the value occurs zero or several times, fail closed and write nothing.
input_class: Structurally real WordprocessingML packages (content types, package/document rels, styles, core properties, optional binary media), 1-12 paragraphs, 1-5 runs each, random run properties, xml:space=preserve, Unicode and XML-special characters; target occurs once (70 %), never (15 %) or 2-3 times (15 %); replacement may be empty but never equals the target.
scope_limits: NO replacement of text spanning several runs or text nodes
NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, comments, headers/footers or numbering guarantees
NO general DOCX editing; one exact text node per call
NO no-op edits: new == old fails closed by design and is outside the input class

declared.lineage: derived from the claim and the OOXML structure; regex/minidom code path, never ElementTree

falsification_condition: Any generated package on which a unique target is not replaced exactly once with all other members byte-identical, or on which a non-unique target does not fail closed without output.
history: Component of the ARTIFACT_CREATION family route (Brain-owned DOCX skills); never measured on fresh instances before 2026-10-14. First measurement found a real defect: replacement by the empty string always failed closed (ROUNDTRIP_CONTENT_MISMATCH, 18 % of instances); fixed the same day by comparing re-parsed text as (text or ''). Two oracle corrections were also needed (namespace-aware text extraction; inverse edit not applicable for empty replacement) - recorded here because the test must be as true as the solver.
